results.content: Recent work has shown that training a mixture of policies, as opposed to a single one, that are driven to explore different regions of the state-action space can address this shortcoming by generating a diverse set of behaviors, referred to as skills, that can be collectively used to great effect in adaptation tasks or for hierarchical planning. Through an extensive empirical evaluation comparing eight state-of-the-art algorithms (four flagship algorithms from each line of work) on the basis of (i) metrics directly evaluating the skills' diversity, (ii) the skills' performance on adaptation tasks, and (iii) the skills' performance when used as primitives for hierarchical planning; QD methods are found to provide equal, and sometimes improved, performance whilst being less sensitive to hyperparameters and more scalable. In this environment, we demonstrate that by learning a model of long-term progress from expert data containing only observations, we can achieve efficient exploration in challenging sparse tasks, well beyond what is possible with current state-of-the-art approaches.

results.title: Few-shot transfer learning enables robust acoustic ...
results.content: Transfer learning enables community monitoring by adapting pre-trained BirdNET model. We demonstrate the use of few-shot transfer learning as a strategy to efficiently adapt a pre-trained BirdNET source model to a new target domain with minimal local training data. We present an open-source workflow with guidelines to evaluate performance with ecologically meaningful metrics and train a target model with improved or missing classes for biotic and abiotic signals of interest. Few-shot transfer learning leverages the learned knowledge of a pre-trained classifier to enable robust monitoring at the community level across the landscape and offers an approach that can be readily applied to other environments and taxa. Code for the transfer learning workflow, programming examples, and the graphical user interface for ensemble model prediction, as well as all data required for the reproduction of results from this study, are available at the open-source repository github.com/giojacuzzi/few-shot-transfer-learning-bioacoustics (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15694435, Jacuzzi, 2025) which leverages BirdNET-Analyzer (Kahl et al., 2021) as a dependency.
